skill.name: design-spec-extraction
skill.description: Extract structured design specifications from screenshots, Figma exports, UI mockups, and website captures for developer handoff.
skill.summary: Convert visual UI sources into design tokens, component maps, and accessibility notes.
skill.author: Cygnusfear

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by markdown examples, design terminology, schema URLs, and local JSON output paths. Two findings are confirmed because the skill asks users to run a local mkdir command with a project-derived directory name; no evidence of remote exfiltration, prompt injection, or malicious intent was found.

remediation.issue: External shell command for output directory creation
remediation.suggestion: Replace the mkdir -p instruction with a request to use the Write tool to create files under a clearly named local .design-specs directory, or require users to confirm the directory name before any shell command is run.
State that outputs must stay under .design-specs/{project} and that project names should use simple alphanumeric, dash, or underscore characters.

content.value_statement: Manual design handoff from screenshots can miss tokens, spacing, and component details. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through a multi-pass extraction process that creates structured design specifications.
actual_capabilities: Extracts layout regions, grids, containers, and source metadata from visual UI inputs.
Identifies color palettes, semantic color roles, typography scales, spacing, and dimensions.
Maps visible UI elements into a hierarchical component tree with bounds and confidence notes.
Captures accessibility observations, contrast concerns, touch targets, and interaction states.
Consolidates intermediate pass outputs into a W3C Design Tokens Community Group style JSON specification.
limitations: Requires a screenshot, mockup, Figma export, or similar visual source from the user.
Cannot guarantee exact pixel values when the source image is low resolution or compressed.
Cannot observe hidden interactions unless separate state images or context are provided.
Writes local intermediate files as part of the documented workflow.

use_cases.title: Create implementation-ready design handoff
use_cases.description: Turn a static UI screenshot into tokens, component bounds, and layout notes before building the interface.

use_cases.title: Document an existing interface
use_cases.description: Extract reusable color, typography, spacing, and component patterns from current product screens.

use_cases.title: Compare design consistency
use_cases.description: Analyze mockups for repeated patterns, spacing scales, and accessibility issues before handoff.

prompt_templates.title: Extract a simple screenshot
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the design-spec-extraction skill on the attached screenshot. Create a concise design specification with layout, colors, typography, components, and accessibility notes.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a developer handoff
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this UI mockup with the full multi-pass workflow. Save intermediate files under .design-specs/product-screen and produce the final design-spec output for frontend implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a design system screen
prompt_templates.prompt: Extract design tokens and component patterns from this screen. Emphasize semantic token names, reusable components, spacing scale, and confidence scores.

prompt_templates.title: Consolidate multiple states
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these default, hover, active, and disabled state screenshots. Produce one consolidated design spec that documents component variants, accessibility behavior, and token references.

output_examples.input: Landing page screenshot for a new marketing site.
output: Layout regions identified: header, hero, feature grid, testimonial area, and footer.
Design tokens extracted for colors, type scale, spacing, radii, and shadows.
Component catalog produced for buttons, cards, navigation, badges, and content sections.
Accessibility notes include contrast checks and touch target concerns.
Grid and sidebar structure documented with estimated bounds.
Semantic colors mapped for background, surface, text, actions, and status indicators.
Tables, filters, metric cards, and charts listed as component groups.
Confidence report highlights areas where exact values need designer confirmation.

best_practices: Use the highest resolution image available so color and spacing estimates are more accurate.
Provide separate screenshots for important responsive breakpoints and interaction states.
Validate the final output against the included schema before using it for automation.
anti_patterns: Do not expect exact source design tokens from a compressed screenshot alone.
Do not mix unrelated screens in one extraction unless you want a shared design system summary.
Do not run shell commands with unreviewed project names or paths.

faq.question: What inputs work best?
faq.answer: High-resolution screenshots, Figma exports, UI mockups, and website captures work best. Clear images improve token and spacing accuracy.

faq.question: Does it generate production code?
faq.answer: No. It produces structured design specifications that developers can use for implementation or code generation workflows.

faq.question: Can it identify accessibility issues?
faq.answer: Yes. It can note visible contrast concerns, touch target sizes, focus states, and semantic structure limits from the provided visuals.

faq.question: Does it access live websites?
faq.answer: No. The skill is designed for user-provided visual inputs, not browsing or scraping live websites.

faq.question: Why does it use multiple passes?
faq.answer: Separate passes reduce missed details by focusing on layout, colors, typography, components, spacing, states, and consolidation.

faq.question: Is the output exact?
faq.answer: The output is an informed extraction with confidence notes. Exact values may need confirmation from original design files.
